concept.name: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo
concept.definition: Goichi Hosoda's 'one-look equilibrium chart' (published 1969): a five-line system of high-low midpoint averages - Conversion Line, Base Line, two Leading Spans forming the cloud (Kumo), and a Lagging Span - designed to show trend, momentum, and support/resistance at a glance.
concept.intuition: Price above the cloud means uptrend, below means downtrend, inside means no trend; the cloud projected ahead sketches where support or resistance is expected to lie.
concept.mechanics: Tenkan-sen = midpoint of the 9-period high-low; Kijun-sen = 26-period midpoint; Senkou A = average of the two, plotted 26 bars ahead; Senkou B = 52-period midpoint, also 26 ahead; Chikou = close plotted 26 back. Signals combine price/cloud position, cloud color (A vs B), Tenkan-Kijun crosses, and price-Kijun crosses.
concept.formula: Tenkan = (max(H,9)+min(L,9))/2; Kijun = (max(H,26)+min(L,26))/2; Senkou A = (Tenkan+Kijun)/2 shifted +26; Senkou B = (max(H,52)+min(L,52))/2 shifted +26; Chikou = Close shifted -26.
concept.failure_modes: Midpoint averages lag like all trend tools and whipsaw in ranges; the cloud shifted 'into the future' is computed entirely from past data and is not a forecast.
concept.misconceptions: Ichimoku is an analytical framework, not a proven predictive system - and the 9/26/52 defaults reflect the 1960s Japanese six-day trading week, not universal constants.
concept.example: 9-day high 55, low 51: Tenkan-sen = 53; with a 26-day midpoint of 50, Senkou A plotted 26 days ahead = 51.5.
